DERIVED — The shared hub is a poor place for repository-specific quality settings: its router selects workflow modes and bundles surface packets as read-only evidence, while its registry defines workflow and surface axes. Editing those files for one repository would couple local checklist policy to shared routing and create a hub fork to maintain. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:11] `one workflow mode primary plus zero-or-more surface packets as read-only evidence` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json:18] `packetKind:'surface' entries are read-only domain-evidence packets` [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json:5] `The WORKFLOW axis (sk-code-quality/sk-code-review) is process;`

INFERRED — The lightest no-fork extension is an optional repository-root manifest such as .code-quality.json. It could map repository-relative target patterns to repository-relative checklist files and add local artifact-label patterns while leaving the built-in map and patterns as defaults. This is a proposal, not a current feature; the cost is a schema and loader, path and pattern validation, clear merge and failure rules, checks that both the quality workflow and comment checker read the same file, plus per-repository maintenance. DERIVED — A repository-owned surface packet can hold reusable domain checklists, with the local manifest pointing to those files. The hub can bundle a surface as read-only evidence, but sk-code-quality still treats its own target-path map as authoritative, so automatic selection needs an explicit adapter from target path to packet checklist. This costs more setup than one flat manifest, and fits policies reused across several projects better.
